replies.question: Why does the pencil look bent even though it stays straight?
replies.answer: The pencil looks bent because light travels from the submerged part of the pencil through water and then into air, changing direction at the angled boundary between these two mediums. This change in direction of light, called refraction, makes the straight pencil appear bent to your eyes even though it remains straight.

replies.question: So is the pencil itself physically bent, or does the light change direction?
replies.answer: The pencil is not physically bent; it stays straight. The light changes direction when it passes from water to air at an angle, which makes the pencil look bent to our eyes.
